allOf.description: Inherits shared step-base properties ($schema, id, owner, created_at, canonical_refs_used).

ambiguities.description: Open ambiguities this step could not settle; each names what it is about. An item is deleted once its answer is applied.

milestones.description: Roadmap milestones with user stories and tasks, listed in ascending target_date order (E520 otherwise). The order states no dependency between milestones: a milestone's target_date carries the schedule. Milestone status is not stored here: it lives on the step 16 anchor row.

milestone_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this milestone. Convention: ms-{phase-or-domain}-{noun}. Decision rule: choose a name that reflects the delivered capability, not a sequential position — IDs must remain stable once tasks reference them, so renaming breaks dependency tracking. Examples: 'ms-auth-mvp' (auth domain, first release), 'ms-payment-integration' (payment domain), 'ms-reporting-phase1' (phased delivery with explicit phase suffix). Anti-pattern: 'ms-1' or 'ms-milestone-a' (sequential labels with no traceable meaning); 'ms-all-features' (too broad to manage — split into domain-scoped milestones).

name.description: Human-readable name of the milestone, distinguishable from all other milestones in this roadmap. Use Title Case, 3–6 words describing the major deliverable theme. Examples: 'Core Authentication API', 'Payment Integration MVP', 'User Profile Management', 'Performance Hardening Sprint', 'Data Migration Phase 1'. Avoid sequential labels ('Milestone 1', 'Phase A') — they carry no semantic meaning. Avoid verb phrases ('Implement Auth') — use noun phrases describing the delivered capability.

target_date.description: Target completion date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Decision rule: set target_date to the sprint end date when the milestone aligns to a sprint; use the agreed delivery date from the project plan otherwise. Examples: '2025-03-31' (end of Q1 sprint), '2025-06-15' (negotiated delivery date for a partner integration). Each milestone should have a distinct date that reflects its actual planned completion. Anti-pattern: setting all milestones to the same date — identical dates signal copy-paste from a template rather than a real plan, and make it impossible to sequence or track progress.

risk_status.description: Risk level for this milestone's delivery confidence. Decision rule — 'low': on track, no known blockers; 'medium': risk identified, mitigation in progress, delivery still achievable; 'high': blocker present, delivery at risk without active intervention; 'critical': milestone at risk of failure, escalate to stakeholders immediately. Escalation examples: use 'medium' when a key dependency has slipped by 1 week and a workaround is in progress; use 'high' when a dependency has slipped by 2+ weeks with no confirmed mitigation; use 'critical' when the milestone cannot be delivered in scope without a timeline change decision. Anti-pattern: defaulting to 'low' to avoid escalation — 'medium' and 'high' trigger the review process that surfaces and resolves blockers before they become critical.

user_story.description: User story this milestone addresses. Follow 'As a <role>, I want <goal>, so that <benefit>' to tie the milestone to a user-facing outcome.

task_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this task. It should be unique across the whole spec, not only within the parent milestone: the same `task_id` in two milestones is reported as E704. Use the pattern 'task-{verb}-{noun}' to make the ID self-describing. Examples: 'task-implement-auth-endpoint', 'task-add-session-schema', 'task-write-login-unit-tests', 'task-deploy-auth-service', 'task-configure-rate-limiting'. The verb names the work type (implement, add, write, migrate, configure, deploy, integrate). Avoid sequential IDs like 'task-1' or 'task-a' — they convey no meaning and break traceability when tasks are reordered.

description.description: What this task accomplishes, at the granularity of a developer story. Describe the user-facing or system-observable outcome, not implementation steps. Scope: one coherent piece of work completable in 1–3 days. Examples: 'Implement POST /auth/login endpoint with JWT issuance and rate limiting', 'Add users table migration with bcrypt password column and soft-delete support', 'Write unit tests for token refresh logic covering expiry and invalid-signature boundary conditions', 'Configure Stripe webhook handler to transition order status on payment confirmation'. Avoid: single-word descriptions ('Implement'), pure technical micro-steps ('Add index'), or commit-message-level details.

acceptance_criteria.description: Conditions that must be met for this task to be considered complete. Each criterion should be objectively verifiable — write them so a reviewer who wasn't present can confirm completion. Examples: 'All unit tests pass with >80% coverage', 'API endpoint responds within 200ms under load test'. Avoid: 'code reviewed', 'looks good', 'done'.

criterion_id.description: Kebab-case identifier of this task criterion. It should be unique across the whole spec and should not reuse a step 04 criterion id (suggested prefix: 'tc-'). Examples: 'tc-confirm-expired-token', 'tc-confirm-reused-token'. Anti-pattern: 'tc-1' (a sequential label that carries no meaning).

text.description: Full text of the acceptance criterion (minimum 15 characters). Decision rule: each criterion should cover a distinct scenario type — happy path, error case, or boundary condition — so that together they provide full coverage of the task's behavior. Happy path example: 'All unit tests pass and line coverage is >= 80%.' Error case example: 'POST /checkout with an expired payment token returns HTTP 402 with error code PAYMENT_EXPIRED.' Boundary condition example: 'A cart with exactly 100 items processes without timeout under nominal load.' Anti-pattern: criteria that only describe happy paths — error cases and boundary conditions must also be specified to prevent regressions.

refines.description: Ids of the obligations this criterion narrows: the one it makes testable at task level. When several nodes state the same rule, name the most downstream system or delivery node. Required unless the criterion carries removes. Example: ["ac-password-reset-3"]. Anti-pattern: naming a fixture here (use verified_by).

removes.description: Ids of deleted nodes whose removal this criterion checks. The criterion is justified by the removed id; the id need not exist any more. A criterion must carry refines or removes. Optional.

verified_by.description: Ids of the fixtures, CI jobs or rules that prove this criterion. Optional. Example: ["fix-password-reset-expired-token"].

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this criterion: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former ids of this criterion; `specdev node rename` adds the old id here. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this criterion replaces. Optional.

items.description: A single task criterion covering one scenario type (happy path, error case or boundary condition). It refines the obligation it narrows, or removes a deleted one, and may name the verifiers that prove it.

environment_ref.description: Canonical reference to the target environment for this task. Kind must be 'environment'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:environment:staging", "kind": "environment", "label": "staging"}. Use to indicate which environment this task targets for deployment or testing. Common IDs: 'cn:core:environment:dev', 'cn:core:environment:staging', 'cn:core:environment:prod'.

metric_ref.description: Canonical reference to the metric used to measure task completion. Kind is structurally pinned to 'metric'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:metric:error-rate", "kind": "metric", "label": "Error Rate"}. Use when task completion is gated on a measurable metric (e.g., performance benchmark, coverage threshold). Omit for tasks with qualitative acceptance criteria only.

depends_on.description: Ids of the tasks of this roadmap that must be done before this task. Optional. The tasks of the roadmap must not form a cycle (E703). Example: ["task-add-reset-token-table"].

disposition.description: Why this task is deliberately not being built now. Absent for a task that is planned. value 'deferred' postpones the task under a named condition; 'wont_do' cancels it for good. The reason is required: name the blocker or decision and, for 'deferred', the condition to resume. Progress is not stored here: it is computed. Example: {"value": "deferred", "reason": "Blocked on vendor sandbox credentials; resume once they are granted."}. Anti-pattern: deleting a task to dodge a coverage finding (deletion loses the record that the work was considered).

value.description: 'deferred': postponed, will resume under the named condition. 'wont_do': permanently cancelled.

reason.description: Why the task is deferred or cancelled; for 'deferred' also the condition to resume. Anti-pattern: 'TBD' or 'not doing this'.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this task: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former ids of this task; `specdev node rename` adds the old id here. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this task replaces. Optional.

items.description: A single task of a milestone with its acceptance criteria. Each criterion narrows an obligation or proves it; the task's progress and the FRs it addresses are computed.

tasks.description: Atomic sub-tasks required to complete the user story.

risks.description: Known risks that could delay or block this milestone. Each entry should name the specific threat, its probability, and the planned mitigation. Decision rule: write one entry per distinct risk, not one entry per category. Examples: 'Third-party payment API instability — high probability during peak load; mitigate with circuit breaker and fallback to manual processing order queue.' 'Legal review for PII data policy may miss Sprint 3 deadline — medium probability; mitigate by requesting review in Sprint 2 with a two-week buffer.' Anti-pattern: 'Technical risks' or 'Integration risks' (category labels, not named risks — a reviewer cannot act on a category). Write no node id into the text.

spikes.description: Time-boxed technical investigations required to resolve specific uncertainties before work can proceed. Decision rule: each spike entry must name (1) the question being answered, (2) the time budget, and (3) the expected output. Examples: 'Evaluate Redis Cluster vs Elasticache for session store — 2-day spike, output: architectural decision record with latency benchmarks.' 'Prototype JWT rotation with zero-downtime rollover — 1-day spike, output: working proof of concept committed to feature branch.' Anti-pattern: 'Investigate performance' or 'Research options' (open-ended spikes with no time box or defined output cannot be completed or reviewed). Write no node id into the text.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this milestone: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former ids of this milestone; `specdev node rename` adds the old id here. Optional.

derives_from.description: Ids of the seeds this roadmap milestone takes content from directly. Optional: list a seed routed to this step, and only for content taken straight from the seed and not through an upstream node.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this milestone replaces. Optional.

items.description: A single roadmap milestone with a user story and its tasks. It stores no links: the design milestones and capabilities it serves are computed from what its task criteria refine.

migration_plan.description: High-level strategy for migrating from existing systems or data. A good migration plan addresses four areas: (1) what is being replaced (legacy system, schema version, or API contract); (2) migration sequence (strangler fig pattern vs. big-bang replacement); (3) rollback plan (how to revert if migration fails); (4) acceptance test for successful migration (how to confirm the migration is complete). Example: 'Migrate auth from session cookies to JWT tokens using strangler fig pattern across 3 milestones — existing session auth remains active until milestone 3; rollback: re-enable session middleware; acceptance: all auth endpoints accept JWT tokens and all legacy session tests pass.' Anti-pattern: 'We will migrate the data' (does not describe sequence, rollback, or acceptance criteria).
